slides.sub: Three days to go. Don't undo months of training at the kitchen table.

slides.title: Trying new food
slides.head: Race week is not the time to experiment.
slides.body: Stick to the meals, gels and drinks you know. A new sports drink at the expo can wait until next week.

slides.title: One huge dinner
slides.head: Spread the carbs over 2 to 3 days.
slides.body: Eat normally and add carbs to each meal. One giant plate on Friday night just leaves you heavy at the 04:00 start.

slides.title: A new breakfast
slides.head: Eat what you ate before your long runs.
slides.body: Early, simple and tested. Race morning is not the day to find out how a new muesli sits.

slides.title: Waiting to be hungry
slides.head: Eat on a schedule, not on a feeling.
slides.body: Start within the first 30 to 45 minutes and keep going. By the time you feel empty, you're already behind.

slides.title: Copying the pros
slides.head: 60 to 90g an hour only if your gut is trained.
slides.body: Many ultra runners aim for that range. If you haven't practised it, go with what worked in training.

slides.title: Skipping refills
slides.head: Fill up fully at every aid station.
slides.body: Wind and warm afternoons dry you out. Leave every aid station with full bottles, and bring your own cup.
